items.text: Do We Actually Need a Smartwatch?
items.article: I still wear an analogue watch quite often. It doesn’t know how many steps I’ve taken, how well I slept or whether I’m stressed. It has never congratulated me for standing up, and it certainly doesn’t vibrate because somebody has sent “Good Morning" to a WhatsApp group. But smartwatches are everywhere now, which makes me wonder: do we actually need them, or have we simply become used to having another screen attached to our bodies? From what I see around me, most people wearing smartwatches aren’t studying HRV, recovery scores or detailed health trends. Many probably couldn’t tell you what half those measurements mean. What almost everybody understands is one wonderfully simple number: Somewhere along the way, walking became a competitive sport. The watch says 9,643 steps at 10.30 at night and suddenly somebody is pacing around the bedroom because apparently going to sleep with 357 steps outstanding would be an admission of defeat.
